learn by heart verb

also memorise, memorize, have down pat, you have it down pat, commit to memory, memorise (a text)

classical

Traupman 30
Cic.
Traupman 338

ēdiscō, ēdiscere, ēdidicī

verb, third conjugation

Other words

  • memoriae mandāre — commit to memory, learn

    phrase: mandāre with the dative memoriae · classical · Cic. Lael. 1.3: ejus disputātiōnis sententiās memoriae mandāvī (Lewis & Short s.v. is); Cic. Lael. 1.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. brevis); Traupman 344

    Cicero’s phrase for “commit to memory”: memoriae mandāre, to hand over to the memory. Ēdiscere is to learn a text off by heart.

  • memoriā comprehendere — hold in the memory, commit to memory

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.154 (Lewis & Short s.v. memoria)

  • memoriae committere — commit to memory

    avoid · modern · Traupman 103: to commit to memory, memoriae committere

    Traupman’s phrase, an English calque that Lewis & Short does not quote; Cicero says memoriae mandāre (above).

Examples

  • Ōrdine omnem rem tenēs.

    You have the whole thing down pat.Traupman 97
